ladders.title: The core loop
ladders.description: Dig down, haul ore home, sell it, buy a better pod, go deeper. Fuel is the clock and the deep hits back. This is the first pillar, the upgrade loop.

ladders.title: Money, fuel and spoil
ladders.description: Ore becomes money at the processor; money becomes parts, fuel and repairs. Rock the drill used to destroy becomes spoil, then slag brick, then new salvage crates.

ladders.title: The ore ladder
ladders.description: Seven ores, cheap to dear. All seven are in layer 1 and below, rarer in the deep zones. Cicatrium is the catalyst, not a sale.

ladders.title: Bootstrap: salvage to the first run
ladders.description: There is no tree and no ore on the surface. Salvage crates and fungal stalks give wood and metal; the metal builds the terminal parts; the terminals bring the colony back; the Mole goes down.

ladders.title: The colony's terminals
ladders.description: Each terminal is a Company machine, dead until its parts go in, and the repairs form a chain. One repair serves every charter in the world.

ladders.title: The Employee Handbook
ladders.description: Nine chapters of directives that tick off by themselves as you play, then Notes found in the world. It teaches the rules; the world stays a mystery.

ladders.title: Layers, breaches and the story
ladders.description: A chain of layers, each with three zones, joined by breach crusts. Layers 1 and 2 exist; the rest of the eight story layers, the Ramp and the uncharted worlds are planned.

ladders.title: Charters, crews and accounts
ladders.description: A charter is the crew's company: its own account, pods, parts and story. Friendly, never PvP.

ladders.title: The colony: Prosperity
ladders.description: A derelict Company mining town built once at the spawn, with a ring of salvage around it and the Conduit running down from it.

ladders.title: The pod chassis ladder
ladders.description: Each chassis is generally better than the one before but leans somewhere, so older ones keep a job. Each caps the tier of its parts.

ladders.title: Drill
ladders.description: Faster boring, from the stock tricone to the sixth tier. Each tier changes the cutter on the front.

ladders.title: Hull
ladders.description: More hull to take lava, gas, crust and hard landings.

ladders.title: Engine
ladders.description: More thrust for the rotor and treads.

ladders.title: Fuel tank
ladders.description: A bigger tank buys a longer dive.

ladders.title: Radiator
ladders.description: Cuts the heat the hull takes from lava; a vital part from the Magma Belt down.

ladders.title: Cargo bay
ladders.description: More ore slots, so more per trip.

ladders.title: Scanner
ladders.description: Range and what it can see: ore, then lava, then gas.

ladders.title: Lights
ladders.description: Pod lights are the only light below the surface; a brighter lamp lights more of the dark and keeps the Retained away.

ladders.title: Lava and its counters
ladders.description: Lava floods a bore through layer rock. The pod shields its pilot, so the hull is what lava costs. The ladder: see it, line the shaft by hand, line it automatically, hear it come, then shrug it off.

ladders.title: Gas and its counters
ladders.description: Gas pockets look like stone and blast the hull when the drill opens them; damage grows with depth. Steer round them, hear them, then bleed them.

ladders.title: Company Rock and its counters
ladders.description: Company Rock is a block in the layers that the drill refuses and a hand breaks only at a ruinous cost. A pilot can steer round it for free, or buy a blasting charge to clear it and keep a straight shaft; a shaped charge clears a whole column of it, and a Prospector's best drill bites it slowly.

ladders.title: The Retained and other creatures
ladders.description: The Retained are tall, thin, lampless figures that come to dark pods and drain their fuel. They never attack. Lights keep them away, and a grab ends only when the figure is killed: by the pod's drill, or a sword on foot. Below them, every creature is drawn by one thing: things drawn to the dark take, things drawn to the drill hurt, and things drawn to the haul eat.

ladders.title: Darkness and sight
ladders.description: Below the surface there is no sky. An unlit cave is almost black, a stranded pod goes dark, and the Company's cheerful signs explain less the deeper you go.

ladders.title: The breach crust and hard landings
ladders.description: The hull is the pod's life. A fall, a crust and the layers' hazards all spend it; a pod with none left is a wreck.

ladders.title: Stranded, rescue and the way home
ladders.description: Fuel is the clock. Running dry strands the pod, and a pod with no hull is a wreck. Getting back up is staged: carried fuel, tow lines, emergency teleports, then outposts and pads.

ladders.title: The repair station's shelf
ladders.description: Single-use items bought at the repair station. Cheap tools first, then emergency ways home.

ladders.title: Crew roles and seats
ladders.description: The goal is crew, not passengers: each extra seat should have a real-time job that helps, and a pilot can do a weaker version alone. Passengers are allowed until the jobs exist. Provisional until a playtest.

ladders.title: Cockpit, screens and HUD
ladders.description: Everything the player reads: the pod's gauges, the scanner map, the green-screen terminals, the handbook. All of it is resource-pack data, so a pack can restyle it.

ladders.title: Look and sound
ladders.description: Prosperity at dusk: a rust-red world under a slow dusk, 16 pixel textures drawn from recipes, GeckoLib pods and placeholder sound.

nodes.title: Start in Prosperity
nodes.summary: You spawn in a run-down Company mining town on a bare red plain, with a dead pod in the hangar.

nodes.title: Get a pod running
nodes.summary: Gather salvage, repair the terminals and the founding Mole.

nodes.title: Drive and drill down
nodes.summary: Steered like a vanilla boat: W forward, S reverse, A and D turn, with a chase camera. Until limp mode its cruise outruns a sprinting player and its sprint outruns a sprint-jumping one; sprint with W runs it 40% faster for more fuel. Treads on the ground, a rotor to fly, a drill that squares to the grid and bores down and sideways, never up; sprint never speeds the drill.

nodes.title: Fuel is the clock
nodes.summary: Fuel drains all the time and faster when drilling. The stock tank is about four minutes of mixed play, a first trip 40 blocks down and home with fuel to spare; running dry strands the pod.

nodes.title: Scan for ore
nodes.summary: The scanner is a side-view map of the rock around the pod, ore as bright dots.

nodes.title: Haul ore in the cargo bay
nodes.summary: Ore is heavy and non-stacking: carried on foot it slows you, shown as an Ore/Fuel status (fuel weighs too, #1280), an ore tooltip and a one-time line on your first ore; a full bay and the pilot's pack (ore too) cut the lift, and past the climb limit the pod cannot climb: the cockpit's load gauge and OVERLOADED lamp show it, and a jump says so and tells the pilot to dump some.

nodes.title: Fly home
nodes.summary: Drive or fly back up the shaft before the fuel runs out.

nodes.title: Sell at the ore processor
nodes.summary: Park by the processor; the ore pays into the charter's account.

nodes.title: Buy better parts
nodes.summary: Money buys tiered pod parts at the upgrade terminal.

nodes.title: Go deeper
nodes.summary: A stronger pod bores through the breach into the next layer, where the ore pays more and the hazards bite harder.

nodes.title: The deep fights back
nodes.summary: Lava, gas, Company Rock, the crust, darkness and the Retained, each with a ladder of counters.

nodes.title: Ore in the cargo bay
nodes.summary: Mined ore rides home as heavy items; only our ore counts as cargo.

nodes.title: Sell ore for money
nodes.summary: The processor pays a fixed base price per ore.

nodes.title: Spoil
nodes.summary: With a spoil hopper the drill keeps one spoil for each block of waste rock; the bay holds 64.

nodes.title: Work orders
nodes.summary: The Company posts orders (deliver 10 bronzium) that pay a bonus and move the story; later ones repeat.

nodes.title: The charter's account
nodes.summary: One shared pot of money for the whole crew.

nodes.title: Withdraw ore from the cargo
nodes.summary: Move ore from a parked pod's cargo to your pack for no money: the ore the hazard units are crafted from. A kept ore is a sale given up.

nodes.title: Press spoil into salvage crates
nodes.summary: The processor presses spoil into new salvage crates, so wood and scrap renew.

nodes.title: Slag brick
nodes.summary: The processor fuses 2 spoil into 1 brick for no money; bricks line shafts against lava.

nodes.title: Buy repairs and consumables
nodes.summary: Hull nanobots, dynamite, explosives, teleport items and a reserve tank at the repair station.

nodes.title: Buy fuel at the pump
nodes.summary: Early fuel is crafted; later it is bought at the fuel pump.

nodes.title: Buy pod parts
nodes.summary: Tier 2 and up of every part. Tier 1 of every part is crafted.

nodes.title: Catalysts
nodes.summary: Every chassis and every couple of tiers also needs a rare material from one layer; Cicatrium is the first.

nodes.title: Records board
nodes.summary: One entry per charter at the colony: deepest breach, wealth hauled, wrecks salvaged.

nodes.title: Registration fees grow
nodes.summary: Each extra pod a charter registers costs more, so a free second Mole is no cheap deep miner.

nodes.title: Ironium
nodes.summary: $30 an ore. Many small brown chunks. The baseline.

nodes.title: Bronzium
nodes.summary: $60 an ore. Two fat orange domes.

nodes.title: Silverium
nodes.summary: $100 an ore. A thin thread with two pale crystals.

nodes.title: Goldium
nodes.summary: $250 an ore. A thread that swells into one bright nugget.

nodes.title: Platinium
nodes.summary: $750 an ore. Two thick lilac-white bars.

nodes.title: Einsteinium
nodes.summary: $2000 an ore. Two teal crystals in dark hollows.

nodes.title: Cicatrium
nodes.summary: $1500 an ore. A red scar with a wound in it. The catalyst for chassis restores; it is not sold.

nodes.title: Fungal stalks
nodes.summary: Pale stalks on crater floors and in patches among the crates are the wood: press to planks, burn for heat, char to charcoal.

nodes.title: Great stalk
nodes.summary: Rarely a stalk grows huge: three thin trunks braided round each other, with a shelf jutting off each, worth a whole stack of wood. Break a trunk and it comes down, shelves and all, while the others stand.

nodes.title: Stalk collapse
nodes.summary: Break any block of a stalk and everything above it bursts at once, like sugar cane, in a pale spore puff with a wet cough, the drops scattering. Only atmosphere: it never hurts you.

nodes.title: Salvage crates
nodes.summary: Company crates in a ring 100 to 160 blocks out; break one for planks, sticks, cloth, scrap and redstone.

nodes.title: Company rations
nodes.summary: Free sealed tins so a new player does not starve: three at the start, two in each ore car still on the track, one on every use of the canteen, and now and then in a crate.

nodes.title: Stalk mash
nodes.summary: A fungal stalk cooks into a poor meal on a campfire or in a smoker, so food does not run out.

nodes.title: Salvage cloth
nodes.summary: Cloth from a crate; it crafts into string.

nodes.title: The phonograph
nodes.summary: Craft one from planks, iron and copper; a wax cylinder in it plays, an empty hand stops it, and sneaking takes the cylinder out.

nodes.title: Wax cylinders
nodes.summary: Old voices on wax, found in wreck lockers and rarely in salvage crates; each is one recording, shown by its title and year. Some are the oldest phonautograms, others later recordings of a toast, a counting, a soliloquy and a cornet and piano. Never crafted.

nodes.title: Scrap iron and copper
nodes.summary: The crate's metal; melted one for one in a furnace.

nodes.title: Melt scrap in a furnace
nodes.summary: Planks burn to melt scrap into iron and copper ingots.

nodes.title: Tools, a table and a torch
nodes.summary: Handbook chapter 1: craft stone tools, then make a light (a torch from a charred stalk, or a lantern).

nodes.title: Craft the terminal parts
nodes.summary: Ten crafted parts, from iron, copper and redstone, repair the four colony terminals.

nodes.title: Repair the terminals in order
nodes.summary: Pump, processor, upgrade terminal, repair station, each once per world. Drag or shift-click each part into its slot on the dead terminal's screen; a part in stays in.

nodes.title: Craft the Mole's parts
nodes.summary: A drill head, a fuel injector, a rotor hub and a tread assembly bring the founding Mole back.

nodes.title: Craft the first scanner
nodes.summary: Craft a scanner unit from 4 iron, 2 copper and 2 redstone and use it on your pod: that fits the tier 1 scanner. The terminal does not sell tier 1.

nodes.title: Craft the first-tier parts
nodes.summary: Craft a unit for any part from salvage iron, copper and redstone, and for the lights, hopper, brace, sounder, liner, heat shield and console some ore too, which you withdraw from your pod's cargo at the ore processor instead of selling it. Use it on your pod: that fits the tier 1 part. The terminal does not sell tier 1; tier 2 and up are purchases.

nodes.title: Repair the founding Mole
nodes.summary: The first charter fixes the hangar's Mole; the Company advances the pod.

nodes.title: The first run
nodes.summary: Refuel, scan, drill layer 1, sell, buy a first part.

nodes.title: Contract terminal
nodes.summary: Works from the start: found a charter or sign on as crew.

nodes.title: Fuel pump
nodes.summary: Sells fuel to a parked pod. The first repair.

nodes.title: Ore processor
nodes.summary: Buys ore, lets you keep ore from a pod's cargo, fuses slag brick, presses crates, lists work orders.

nodes.title: Upgrade terminal
nodes.summary: Sells tiered pod parts.

nodes.title: Repair station
nodes.summary: Mends the hull and sells consumables.

nodes.title: Hangar console
nodes.summary: Founds the Mole, restores wrecks into pods and buys a refurbished Mole for later charters.

nodes.title: Parked pod uses the terminal
nodes.summary: Park a pod beside a terminal and it works on the pod, not on the player.

nodes.title: Outpost terminals
nodes.summary: A fuel pump and a sell terminal in the outpost hall at the layer 1 floor: fuel costs double and ore pays four fifths of the colony's price.

nodes.title: The handbook item
nodes.summary: Given to every player on joining (before any charter), bound to you, opened with H. The advancements key (L) and the pause menu's Handbook button open it too; vanilla's advancements and toasts are gone.

nodes.title: 1. Welcome to Prosperity
nodes.summary: Gather wood, craft tools, gather scrap, smelt iron, craft a scanner unit.

nodes.title: 2. Bringing Prosperity Back Online
nodes.summary: Repair the pump, the processor and the upgrade terminal.

nodes.title: 3. Meet the Mole
nodes.summary: Repair the Mole and board it.

nodes.title: 4. Fuel Is Life
nodes.summary: Refuel, fly, drill down and return to the colony.

nodes.title: 5. Every Sale Counts
nodes.summary: Sell ore, buy a component, install it.

nodes.title: 6. Seeing Below
nodes.summary: Install the scanner and find ore with it.

nodes.title: Hazards on higher scanners
nodes.summary: A handbook line about unseen hazards that a thermal tier shows; its wording is a user pick.

nodes.title: 7. Staying Safe on the Claim
nodes.summary: Repair the hull and reach the Deep Claim.

nodes.title: 8. Your First Breach
nodes.summary: Break through the crust into layer 2.

nodes.title: 9. Recovering Company Property
nodes.summary: Find the Prospector wreck, tow it, restore it, reach layer 2's floor.

nodes.title: Notes
nodes.summary: Miners' scribbles, torn pages and wreck logs found in the world; one found by anyone fills every member's handbook.

nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.summary: The handbook is revised five times as the story turns; tone changes, rules never do.

nodes.title: Quest map
nodes.summary: The handbook's directives as a fixed flowchart per chapter (nothing drags or zooms), with an intro tab and chapter tabs on every page, an index card for each step (the item it asks for with a count, never its ingredients, and a link to its chapter page) and a popup when a step is done. A click on the item opens its recipe in the parts catalogue. A map does not preview the next chapter.

nodes.title: Controls pages
nodes.summary: Four pages after the contents explain the handbook, the parts catalogue, the Mole and the scanner. Each key is named as you have bound it, so a rebind shows.

nodes.title: Pencil paths
nodes.summary: Each Note found draws a path from earlier miners on a pencil sheet after chapter 9; it completes when your charter reaches the place the Note points to: a wreck, a shaft or another Note. No claim button, no reward but the place.

nodes.title: Progress carries into a charter
nodes.summary: Founding or joining a charter keeps what you did before: directive progress, recipe discoveries, found Notes and completed pencil paths.

nodes.title: Parts catalogue
nodes.summary: A Company parts catalogue in the terminals' green CRT look beside the inventory, crafting table and furnaces: a small button where the recipe book's stood (its tooltip names the key) and O show and hide it, and the choice is kept until you leave the world; R for recipes, U for uses, search, favourites, and a craftable-now switch with a count that includes the crafting table's 3x3 recipes, marked with a small table. Long names show whole, and the search, switch, page and open recipe are kept until you leave the world. A click on any item opens its recipes (a right click its uses), never a spec sheet; a FILL GRID switch on the recipe card moves the ingredients into the open 2x2 or 3x3 crafting grid as the vanilla recipe book does, and when you lack some shows the recipe as a ghost with the missing slots marked, or says it needs a crafting table. R and U work over any slot, a chest or the creative inventory included, where the recipe opens on a screen of its own and Escape goes back to the chest. Backspace or a back knob steps back through the recipes looked at, and A or a star on the recipe adds a favourite; the empty favourites row says how. It lists only what your charter knows, and R on an item it knows nothing of says so instead.

nodes.title: Known recipes
nodes.summary: A charter learns a recipe when a quest step asks for the item or a member gets it or an ingredient; the server sends only those. Unknown recipes still craft.

nodes.title: Only what the world yields
nodes.summary: A recipe that needs or makes an item this world has none of is disabled, vanilla's included, and the catalogue and the creative tabs leave such items out: "any planks" shows only the woods you can really get.

nodes.title: Spec sheets
nodes.summary: Each Company item has a spec sheet, its page in the parts catalogue: what it is and its ratings, read from the game's own numbers (a part's tiers and prices, a charge's reach, an ore's worth). A small corner slip names it the first time you craft or buy the item, and a key (J) opens the latest; a SPEC SHEET button on the recipe console opens the sheet of any item whose recipe you know. A click on an item never opens a sheet; the sheet has a RECIPES link that shows the item's recipes in the catalogue, and a CLOSE switch.

nodes.title: First-exposure warnings
nodes.summary: A new hazard is warned of the first time you meet it, in plain terms such as PRESSURE EXCEEDS HULL RATING.

nodes.title: Total materials
nodes.summary: M on a recipe in the parts catalogue lists everything it takes in total, through the recipes your charter knows: what you hold, what it takes and what you are short, using what you already hold before breaking anything down. It says when you have it all.

nodes.title: Quest map on terminals
nodes.summary: Colony and outpost terminals show the same map in green-screen style.

nodes.title: The surface
nodes.summary: Regolith plains, craters and terraced mesas under a dusk sky that never reaches day. The loose regolith skin falls like sand; the packed layer and rock under it hold. No ore, no trees.

nodes.title: Layer 1: The Claim
nodes.summary: Dirt and stone, the first ores and the previous miners' shafts. Caves open up as you go down: a few pockets under the surface, more fissures and passages toward the Deep Claim. Teaches the loop.

nodes.title: Topsoil Claims
nodes.summary: The top third of layer 1, in olive hardpan: sparse caves.

nodes.title: Stone Benches
nodes.summary: The middle third of layer 1, in rust-brown packed shale, with a thin bed of it in the hardpan above the contact.

nodes.title: Deep Claim
nodes.summary: The bottom third of layer 1, in cold black shale, where lava starts and the caves are most common.

nodes.title: Abandoned shafts
nodes.summary: Hand-dug shafts of the first generation, about one in ten chunks of layer 1: stalk-plank timbering, a ladder with rungs gone, candle niches with burnt-out stubs and, deeper down more often, a prayer card; a lunch pail at the foot. Some cut through caves.

nodes.title: Cave finds in the Claim
nodes.summary: Seams of ore on the walls of layer 1's caves and shafts, the richer ores more often than in the rock, and now and then a few salvage crates on a cave floor.

nodes.title: Structures in the layers
nodes.summary: Shafts with Note niches, a punch clock, a gallery with a quota board, rails and timbering, and wreck sites.

nodes.title: The first breach
nodes.summary: A crust at the layer's floor: any drill gets through, slowly, hot and hurt. A rumble and a transmission mark the crossing.

nodes.title: Deepest point
nodes.summary: A charter's deepest point sets which orders and transmissions open.

nodes.title: Transmissions
nodes.summary: The story arrives as green-screen messages that fire once per charter, mostly at its deepest point.

nodes.title: Layer 2: The Old Workings
nodes.summary: Collapsed mine levels, rails, a salvageable Prospector wreck, garbled transmissions.

nodes.title: Layer rock and lava look
nodes.summary: Layers 1 and 2 have their own fine-grained rock, rust-brown and grey-green, that runs on across block edges like vanilla stone. Lava flows and glows, and steel beams that meet at a right angle meet with no gap.

nodes.title: Upper Levels
nodes.summary: The top third of layer 2.

nodes.title: Shift Change
nodes.summary: The middle third of layer 2, where Cicatrium first appears.

nodes.title: Prospector's Run
nodes.summary: The bottom third of layer 2, with the Prospector wreck.

nodes.title: Breach crossing with no teleport
nodes.summary: Crossing a breach is a pure dig, with a rumble and a transmission: nobody is moved, because the surface and the layers are one world.

nodes.title: Old worlds refuse to start
nodes.summary: Every world carries a format stamp. From the campaign-world release, a world made before it will not open, and says so with a message instead of losing anything. Start a new world.

nodes.title: One tall campaign world
nodes.summary: The surface and story layers share one dimension, each a Y band with its own light and fog.

nodes.title: Layer 3: Fungal Hollows
nodes.summary: Huge caverns held up by basalt columns, three levels deep: the Garden, the Spore Fields and the Quiet. Cold glowcaps are its only light.

nodes.title: The Garden
nodes.summary: The top third of layer 3: the first natural light, glowcaps on every floor and pale stalks, now and then a great stalk.

nodes.title: The Spore Fields
nodes.summary: The middle third of layer 3, hazy with drifting spores and cold glints, where the rock holds the layer's most gas pockets.

nodes.title: The Quiet
nodes.summary: The bottom third of layer 3: the widest hall, few columns, little glow, and no drone or music.

nodes.title: Columnar basalt
nodes.summary: Every rock face open to a cavern of layer 3 is lined with hexagonal basalt columns; behind them the rock is plain dark basalt, so a gap between columns never shows through.

nodes.title: Glowcaps
nodes.summary: Small fungus that glows cold on cavern floors in layer 3, most in the Garden: light to walk by, never enough to see the far wall.

nodes.title: Giant fungi of the Garden
nodes.summary: The Garden's giant fungi grow in three forms mixed together: braided stalks, broad parasols and bracket spires. Only the stalks grow yet.

nodes.title: Layer 4: The Drowned Deep
nodes.summary: Flooded caverns and pressure; the pod needs seals. The lost miners' story plays out.

nodes.title: Layers 5 to 8
nodes.summary: The Lattice, the Magma Belt, the Ossuary and the Furnace, ending at Head Office.

nodes.title: The finale: a choice
nodes.summary: The boss breaks but cannot die; renounce the Controlling Interest to win, or sign and become the Chairman.

nodes.title: The Ramp
nodes.summary: A few hundred blocks where drilling gets exponentially harder; the end of the campaign is obvious.

nodes.title: Seams and the grained crust
nodes.summary: A fast background swap hidden in a vertical-grained crust at a layer boundary, with decoys that look the same. Mid-layer, a plain slab of rock.

nodes.title: Story-layer splicing
nodes.summary: An update adds a new story layer at the seam without touching what is built ('the depths moved').

nodes.title: Uncharted layers
nodes.summary: Endless 2048-tall worlds below the ramp, a bragging-rights grind for the records board.

nodes.title: Found a charter
nodes.summary: Name it at the contract terminal and become its Director; it gets an account.

nodes.title: Parts are company property
nodes.summary: Parts are bound to the charter and serial-numbered; another charter's parts are void.

nodes.title: Sign on as crew
nodes.summary: Apply with an Employment Contract; the Director approves.

nodes.title: Dormant charters
nodes.summary: A charter nobody belongs to goes dormant and keeps its name, account and pods; its former members can revive it.

nodes.title: Serial numbers
nodes.summary: Each pod and part has a world-wide serial; a restored wreck keeps its own number.

nodes.title: Revive at the contract terminal
nodes.summary: The contract terminal lists the dormant charters you once belonged to; REVIVE makes you its Director. Strangers are refused.

nodes.title: A restored wreck keeps its serial
nodes.summary: The famous wreck carries a lore mark and keeps PROSPECTOR-0002 and its name tag when restored; a charter's own Prospectors skip 0002.

nodes.title: Outposts shared
nodes.summary: A charter's Director can open its outposts to other charters at the contract terminal (off by default). A guest's pod is served at the outpost's own prices and the owner takes no cut. Pads follow when pads exist.

nodes.title: Competition between charters
nodes.summary: A later update might add rivalry; today charters are friendly.

nodes.title: The square and the Host
nodes.summary: The Host's statue stands ten blocks tall in the middle of the Pithead Works.

nodes.title: Chapel, bunkhouse and the Lamp and Pick
nodes.summary: The quiet corners of town, with signs and notes.

nodes.title: The hangar
nodes.summary: Holds the founding pod, dark until your charter repairs it.

nodes.title: Offices and the Works
nodes.summary: The pay office, Personnel, the Continuity Office, the ore house and the headframe.

nodes.title: The statue's hands
nodes.summary: A work order puts the Host's hands back.

nodes.title: Company lamps
nodes.summary: The Company's caged sodium lamp, lit or dark; placed by the colony.

nodes.title: The Lamp and Pick's phonograph
nodes.summary: A phonograph on the bar's counter that plays the colony's own cylinders in turn (a talking doll and a nursery rhyme among them, found nowhere else), and cannot be emptied. Rarely, at night, it starts on its own with nobody in the room.

nodes.title: The canteen
nodes.summary: A Company dispenser in the Lamp and Pick gives a ration every time you use it.

nodes.title: The Conduit
nodes.summary: An undiggable Company pipe from the ore processor straight down through every layer to the Furnace. The story's first clue.

nodes.title: The colony kit
nodes.summary: Company building blocks (plates, beams, pipes, rails, signs, glass windows) the town is built from; unbreakable. Every room inside the town has block light, so no monster spawns in one.

nodes.title: Anchor mode and outposts
nodes.summary: A Behemoth that unfolds into a temporary outpost; built outposts with beds and storage.

nodes.title: Mole
nodes.summary: The founding pod: 1 seat, parts up to tier 2, built for layers 1 and 2. 2 blocks wide and 3 tall.

nodes.title: Pod looks
nodes.summary: A GeckoLib model per chassis; the drill tier picks the cutter on the front.

nodes.title: Charter paint
nodes.summary: Pods are painted per charter and the rotor folds out to fly.

nodes.title: Prospector
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 2: 2 seats, parts up to tier 3, up to layer 3.

nodes.title: Restore a wreck into a pod
nodes.summary: Tow a wreck home and pay money plus catalysts at the hangar console.

nodes.title: Badger
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 3 or 4: 2 to 3 seats, adds the operator, leans to the drill.

nodes.title: Bore scales with the chassis
nodes.summary: A bigger pod carves a bigger tunnel, so its cab and bore grow together.

nodes.title: Hauler
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 4 or 5: 3 seats, leans to cargo. Later the tender pod.

nodes.title: Crawler
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 6: 3 to 4 seats, leans to armour against heat and pressure.

nodes.title: Behemoth
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 7: 4 to 6 seats and an anchor mode.

nodes.title: Drill: stock
nodes.summary: The stock tricone cutter. Speed 1x.

nodes.title: Drill tier 1
nodes.summary: Drill speed 1.4x stock. Crafted as a drill unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Drill tier 2
nodes.summary: Stacked rings on the cutter, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Drill tier 3
nodes.summary: Drill speed 2.5x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Drill tier 4
nodes.summary: Drill speed 3.5x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Drill tier 5
nodes.summary: Drill speed 4.75x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Drill tier 6
nodes.summary: Drill speed 6.0x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Hull: stock
nodes.summary: The stock hull. 1x.

nodes.title: Hull tier 1
nodes.summary: Hull 1.7x stock. Crafted as a hull unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Hull tier 2
nodes.summary: Hull 3.0x stock, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Hull tier 3
nodes.summary: Hull 5.0x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Hull tier 4
nodes.summary: Hull 8.0x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Hull tier 5
nodes.summary: Hull 12.0x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Hull tier 6
nodes.summary: Hull 18.0x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Engine: stock
nodes.summary: The stock engine. 1x.

nodes.title: Engine tier 1
nodes.summary: Engine 1.07x stock. Crafted as an engine unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Engine tier 2
nodes.summary: Engine 1.13x stock, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Engine tier 3
nodes.summary: Engine 1.2x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Engine tier 4
nodes.summary: Engine 1.27x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Engine tier 5
nodes.summary: Engine 1.33x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Engine tier 6
nodes.summary: Engine 1.4x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Fuel tank: stock
nodes.summary: The stock 10 litre tank: about four minutes of drilling, driving and climbing.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 1
nodes.summary: Tank 1.5x stock. Crafted as a fuel tank unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 2
nodes.summary: Tank 2.5x stock, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 3
nodes.summary: Tank 4.0x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 4
nodes.summary: Tank 6.0x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 5
nodes.summary: Tank 10.0x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 6
nodes.summary: Tank 15.0x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Radiator: stock
nodes.summary: The stock radiator. Takes all the heat.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 1
nodes.summary: Lava costs 90 percent of stock. Crafted as a radiator unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 2
nodes.summary: Lava costs 75 percent of stock, $1,250. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 3
nodes.summary: Lava costs 60 percent of stock, $5,000. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 4
nodes.summary: Lava costs 40 percent of stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Radiator tier 5
nodes.summary: Lava costs 20 percent of stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Cargo bay: stock
nodes.summary: The stock bay, 7 ore slots.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 1
nodes.summary: 15 ore slots. Crafted as a cargo bay unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 2
nodes.summary: 25 ore slots, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 3
nodes.summary: 40 ore slots, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 4
nodes.summary: 70 ore slots, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 5
nodes.summary: 120 ore slots, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Scanner tier 1
nodes.summary: The first map: ore in range, every cell drawn as a tiny copy of its block's texture, and in a cell too small to read, ore as a bright mark in its own colour. Crafted as a scanner unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal; every later tier is a purchase. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Scanner tier 2
nodes.summary: The thermal tier: lava glows red in its own texture, lava in the wall dim and dark, and its small cells mark ore in bright colours. $500, and tier 1 must be fitted first. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Scanner tier 3
nodes.summary: Gas pockets show on the map. $1,250. The Prospector's tier. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Scanner tier 4
nodes.summary: The widest, clearest map. $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Lights tier 1
nodes.summary: A first lamp, light level 6. Crafted as a lights unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. Lit pods draw no Retained. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Lights tier 2
nodes.summary: Light level 9, $375. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Lights tier 3
nodes.summary: Light level 12, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Lights tier 4
nodes.summary: Light level 15, $3,750. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Lava in the rock
nodes.summary: Pockets of lava from the Deep Claim down; a bore opens the cells beside it and the lava runs in.

nodes.title: The pod shields its pilot
nodes.summary: A seated pilot takes no lava damage; the hull burns instead, 10 a second, with a HULL BURNING readout and a hiss, and the hull glows red-hot like hot metal until it cools.

nodes.title: Spoil hopper
nodes.summary: The 'keep stone' part: the drill keeps spoil for bricks instead of destroying it. Crafted as a spoil hopper unit and fitted by use, never sold.

nodes.title: Hand lining
nodes.summary: Press R from the seat and the pod lays slag brick round the slab while it stands still.

nodes.title: Liner tier 1
nodes.summary: Lines the shaft with brick as the pod drills, every 4 slabs, only where lava can reach. Crafted as a liner unit and fitted by use, never sold; tier 2 is a purchase.

nodes.title: Liner tier 2
nodes.summary: Rings every 3 slabs, also in a fall, and each brick lines more. $1,000. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: The lava watch
nodes.summary: A HUD line and lamp when flowing lava closes on the pod from behind; every pod has it, free.

nodes.title: Heat shield tier 1
nodes.summary: Crafted as a heat shield unit and fitted by use, never sold; tiers 2 and 3 are purchases. While lava touches the pod, burning slag bricks soak its damage at 4 hull a brick, from the rack first and then the pilot's pack. The HUD shows GLAZE HOLDING or GLAZE SPENT.

nodes.title: Heat shield tier 2
nodes.summary: Each slag brick soaks 6 hull of lava, so a full rack buys about 14 seconds. $1,250. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Heat shield tier 3
nodes.summary: Each slag brick soaks 8 hull of lava, and the pilot's pack burns before the rack, so the rack stays for lining. $2,500. A Prospector takes it.

nodes.title: Heat shield, top tier
nodes.summary: With the Crawler, the top tier shrugs off brief lava, and lining becomes optional.

nodes.title: Lining cracks under pressure
nodes.summary: Deep down, a lined shaft decays under lava pressure; a hairline-crack warning gives seconds to re-line before lava tongues in.

nodes.title: The Kells' lined shaft
nodes.summary: An abandoned 2 x 2 shaft at the end of the rail line in Prospector's Run, walled in slag brick where it passes lava, with 2 to 4 gaps where lava still stands; a pod goes down and re-lines them. A few bricks wait at its head. At its foot the crust is broken through: the shaft opens into the roof of layer 3.

nodes.title: Gas pockets
nodes.summary: A pocket that looks like plain stone and blasts the hull when bored, with a bang and a line naming the gas and the hull it cost; the biggest cause of deaths in layer 1.

nodes.title: Dynamite on a slab
nodes.summary: Light dynamite from the seat to clear the slab under the pod, and a pocket the sounder marks in it. Costly.

nodes.title: Seep sounder tier 1
nodes.summary: A SEEPAGE readout counts the slabs down to a pocket and a hiss quickens as the drill nears. Crafted as a sounder unit and fitted by use, never sold; tier 2 is a purchase.

nodes.title: Seep sounder tier 2
nodes.summary: Reaches 4 slabs down and 2 blocks to each side, and bleeds a marked pocket before boring it. $1,000.

nodes.title: Sideways bores spread the blast
nodes.summary: A pod that opens a pocket sideways takes only a share of the blast, per cell of its slab.

nodes.title: Gas on the map
nodes.summary: Scanner tier 3, on the Prospector, draws pockets in its slice; the sounder stays the cheap Mole part.

nodes.title: Company Rock
nodes.summary: Rock the drill refuses. Steer round it (fuel, time, the next pocket) or blast it with a charge, or bite it with the Prospector's best drill, to keep the shaft straight.

nodes.title: Company Rock look
nodes.summary: Company Rock looks like dense, cool rock crazed by shrinkage joints, with a faint survey chevron on one block in five. In layer 2 the joints glow like lava; under a charge the joints widen and burn brighter before the rock goes.

nodes.title: Steer round it
nodes.summary: Step the pod aside and drill on; the scanner shows nothing of it.

nodes.title: Blasting charge
nodes.summary: A $40 charge set from the seat under the pod. After a 3 second fuse it clears Company Rock and the rock round it, and hurts a pod that stays within 3 blocks. About 5 a straight layer 1 shaft.

nodes.title: Shaped charge
nodes.summary: A $100 charge set like the blasting charge. Its blast is directed down: it clears the whole Company Rock column under the pod, up to 8 rows, and stops at the first other block. It will not be set over lava.

nodes.title: A drill that bites Company Rock
nodes.summary: From drill tier 3 (a Prospector's best) the drill bores Company Rock: ten times slower than stone, three times the fuel, and the cutter heats the hull. A Mole never bites; a hull of 20 or less stops it.

nodes.title: Brute-force it by hand
nodes.summary: Any pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, sword or spear breaks one pod-only block in 60 seconds, in any layer. A diamond or netherite tool burns half its durability doing it; a lesser pick is destroyed as the block goes. Nothing drops. A line says a pod drill is the way.

nodes.title: The Retained
nodes.summary: A lampless figure in the open dark of layers 1 and 2, drawn to pods with no lights; about a third carry a small lamp. It never attacks and never speaks.

nodes.title: The grab and the drain
nodes.summary: It walks to a pod within 20 blocks, clings to the hull and drains fuel, never below 5 percent. The grip ends only when the figure dies.

nodes.title: Lights keep them away
nodes.summary: A pod with a lights part draws no Retained. Lights do not free a pod that is already held.

nodes.title: Kill it with the drill
nodes.summary: No fading: a grab ends only when the Retained dies. The cutter bites it while the pod drills rock, and a sword kills it on foot.

nodes.title: More common deep, facing the pod, a helmet lens
nodes.summary: Layer 1 rolls 1 percent and layer 2 5 percent, up to 5 at once; a figure faces the pod it grips; a tiny dim amber lens shines in its helmet.

nodes.title: Layer bosses
nodes.summary: Five bosses in layers 3 to 7, each guarding a chassis wreck or catalyst. They gate the upgrade ladder, not the descent, and each charter fights each one once.

nodes.title: The Chairman
nodes.summary: Phase 1 on foot: he can be hurt only in the crew's own lamp light. Phase 2: Head Office stands up, built from what the charter sold, and only the drill and explosives hurt it. Broken, never killed.

nodes.title: Three families of creature
nodes.summary: Things drawn to the dark take, things drawn to the drill hurt, and in the uncharted, things drawn to the haul eat. Every creature that costs you does so in the pod and on foot.

nodes.title: An empty surface
nodes.summary: No monster lives on the surface, vanilla or ours: the colony's emptiness is the dread.

nodes.title: They cling to people too
nodes.summary: A Retained comes to a person on foot in the dark with no light in either hand, slows them as if they carried ore and drains their hunger down to a floor. A light in hand keeps one off but does not free you; any blow that kills it does. It never deals damage.

nodes.title: Tallies
nodes.summary: Brass Company counting drones that click over ore near the Conduit in layers 1 and 2 and show as a small amber eye. One that trails a pod for about 30 seconds clamps to the cargo hatch and takes the cheapest ore as a quality sample; the cutter breaks it there. On foot it takes an ore you carry, and one blow breaks it. A lit pod, or one inside a burning flare's light, draws none. They drop nothing, and a scanner reads one as ore.

nodes.title: Alarm
nodes.summary: Killing a drifter rings the alarm of its zone for three minutes: more drifters come to the drill, sooner. A deeper drone beats and the readout counts the seconds.

nodes.title: Drifters
nodes.summary: Glowing spore creatures in the Hollows, each a jellyfish, a spore sac or a chain of bulbs, drift toward drill noise and footsteps and burst into spore gas that eats the hull or poisons and blinds. Sonar will read them as empty cave.

nodes.title: Overgrowth
nodes.summary: Bores left unvisited in the Hollows grow over with soft growth. Placed blocks never do, so a lined shaft stays open.

nodes.title: Bolt driver
nodes.summary: A roof-bolter for on foot, bought at the repair station with its bolts. It fires bolts at range, which hurt creatures and break nothing, and sets roof bolts that hold the roof round them against cave-ins.

nodes.title: Thrown flares, decoys and charges
nodes.summary: Bought and thrown by hand on foot. A $12 flare lights the dark and keeps the Retained off a pod or a person on foot, and the Tallies off a pod, for 90 seconds, from the moment it lands, and a $55 charge blasts after a 3 second fuse as the pod's charge does. The $25 decoy rings out for 45 seconds and pulls drifters, and later things drawn to the drill, off the drill toward itself.

nodes.title: Tether
nodes.summary: A $90 line you clip to your pod. It pays out 24 blocks, catches a fall, and its winch hauls you home through open air. Used on a second pod it tows it, a wreck too. The winch is loud.

nodes.title: The Hush
nodes.summary: Layer 3's boss: a membrane in the Quiet's roof lowers toward the loudest noise while the crew frees the Badger wreck on foot and tows it out.

nodes.title: Limpets
nodes.summary: Stone-shelled things seal onto a hull underwater, knock as they settle and crack its seals. The operator's arm pries them off.

nodes.title: The Undertow
nodes.summary: Layer 4's boss: a cavern-sized shape seen only on sonar drags and coils pods in the Basin, where the Lymphium lies. The first true crew fight.

nodes.title: Listeners
nodes.summary: Blind crystal things in the Lattice come to resonance: drilling crystal, pings, charges. They freeze in silence and cut hard.

nodes.title: Echoes
nodes.summary: False sonar contacts in the Lattice: ghost pods and a crew that isn't there. They never act.

nodes.title: The Great Listener
nodes.summary: Layer 5's boss: pods are loud bait while the crew on foot plant charges on its resonant nodes, and every blast calls it.

nodes.title: Recovery units
nodes.summary: In act 3 the Chairman's machines clamp an unauthorised pod, take its cargo and bill you for it. On foot they shackle you and take the ore you carry.

nodes.title: Checkpoint wardens
nodes.summary: Recorded sentries at Checkpoint refuse you and wave you through. They never act.

nodes.title: Scabs
nodes.summary: Lava-dwellers seal a fresh bore near the arteries with hot crust. Lined shafts stay open.

nodes.title: The Bailiff
nodes.summary: Layer 6's boss: a repossession rig drags pods upward while the crew fights to unclamp Roz's Crawler.

nodes.title: THE EYES
nodes.summary: They open in the Ossuary's bone when the lights go off and never attack. While they watch you, nothing drawn to the dark comes near.

nodes.title: Masks
nodes.summary: Old Chairmen's masks scuttle out of the Old Furnaces to the dark and cover a pod's canopy or a person's visor: blindness, a draining lamp, a voice making offers.

nodes.title: The Old Idol
nodes.summary: Layer 7's boss: a cold bronze figure relit by the drill. Only the drill and explosives hurt it, and it eats the cargo it takes.

nodes.title: Gnawers
nodes.summary: In the uncharted layers, things that come to the haul eat ore in the rock, in a bay and in storage, chewing through anything between.

nodes.title: Dreamed remixes
nodes.summary: Each uncharted world dreams one story layer, and its creatures return with one rule warped by the seed.

nodes.title: Sonar reads creatures
nodes.summary: Real things echo, hollow things (the Retained, masks) give none, and Company machines echo as ore. A ping is loud: the Sleeper's walk toward it from up to 48 blocks.

nodes.title: Passive listening
nodes.summary: A silent, short-range sonar mode that hears movement without calling anything.

nodes.title: Charge launcher
nodes.summary: The operator fires bought charges at range: dynamite, plastic, the blasting charge and the shaped charge.

nodes.title: Flare and decoy rounds
nodes.summary: Bought rounds for the charge launcher: a burst of light against things drawn to the dark, or a noise far off that leads things drawn to the drill away.

nodes.title: Sonar burst
nodes.summary: A very loud ping that stuns things drawn to the drill for a few seconds and wakes everything else near.

nodes.title: Company turret
nodes.summary: From layer 6, the operator's rivet turret: good on machines, poor on living things, useless on bronze.

nodes.title: Damped drill head
nodes.summary: A Lattice drill part: crystal rings less as it is drilled, at the cost of drill speed.

nodes.title: Creatures and placed blocks
nodes.summary: Creatures drawn to the drill break exposed blocks not rated for the depth, even while nobody is near. A closed, rated shell keeps everything inside safe.

nodes.title: Damping blocks
nodes.summary: Fungal felt and damped crystal muffle a pad or machine, so things drawn to the drill are not drawn to it.

nodes.title: While nobody is near
nodes.summary: An outpost settles what visited it while it was empty. Built: the Retained drain stored fuel from a dark outpost, and an unloaded outpost keeps its visits until it loads. Still to come: broken unrated blocks and taken ore.

nodes.title: Salvage heap
nodes.summary: What a broken storage block leaves: a heap that keeps everything the block held. Anyone can open it and take the contents; visits never touch it.

nodes.title: Alert and incident report
nodes.summary: When a visit is rolled, every charter member online hears Disturbance reported at Outpost N. The first member to open the outpost's terminal on return gets a typed incident report of what was taken.

nodes.title: Darkness
nodes.summary: Each layer's biome sets its own ambient colour, darker with depth. Until you fit pod lights, a torch or lantern is the light you have.

nodes.title: Pod light ledger
nodes.summary: A pod's light blocks are recorded in a ledger before they are placed, so they move with the pod and clear when it leaves.

nodes.title: A stranded pod goes dark
nodes.summary: With no fuel or hull the pod is powered off, and its lights go out.

nodes.title: Glow and light beams
nodes.summary: Lamps and gauges carry a soft glow in Company amber, and a lit pod's headlamp (warm white) and the colony floodlights (amber) throw a faint cone of light that a wall cuts short. Seen only: the real light is the pod's light block.

nodes.title: Smooth moving light
nodes.summary: An optional dynamic-lights mod and an opt-in shader pack, both written up in the player guide.

nodes.title: The suit lamp
nodes.summary: On foot, a suit lamp on a battery; the finale's Unnumbered Lamp never runs out.

nodes.title: HUD signal decay
nodes.summary: Near the floor of every layer something gets on the line: the scanner fills with noise, then the gauges flicker, jump to false readings and go dark, and in the last slabs the whole display is gone. The hull and burning lamps and the hull alarm never fail.

nodes.title: Console upgrade
nodes.summary: A three-tier part that shrinks the decay toward the floor. Tier 1 is a crafted unit (copper, redstone and a little Bronzium); tiers 2 and 3, $500 and $1,250, are bought. A Mole fits two tiers, and the third (a Prospector's) is immune.

nodes.title: Per-layer drones and the Lamp Hymn
nodes.summary: The surface and each layer hum their own drone: wind and a far metal groan above; sub-bass, slow beating tones, creaks and rare knocks below, no vanilla music. A short reed hymn plays when you found or join a charter, go down a breach and come up into the colony, slower and more worn at each layer; its opening notes mark each handbook chapter you finish, and a terminal you bring back online powers up with a rising chord.

nodes.title: Old voices in the dark
nodes.summary: Deep down, now and then, a faint old voice comes from somewhere out of sight: a syllable, a breath of a scale, half a word. Rare in layer 1, more often and more worn in the Old Workings, broken and slow below, where the oldest and strangest of them are heard: a phonautogram made with a human ear. Never twice the same in a row, never over the hymn.

nodes.title: The Company horn
nodes.summary: A brass public-address horn hung over the punch clock's hall in the Old Workings. Stand near it and the old voices come from it, after a crackle of static: a scale, a train on an elevated railway, a barometer. Scenery: nothing rides on it.

nodes.title: The punch clock that calls the hours
nodes.summary: The Company's punch clock in the Shift Change hall rarely calls an hour in Frank Lambert's 1878 voice, about once an hour of play beside it, and often gets it wrong: another hour, or the hour before and the one after with the true one missing. Deeper, slowed, broken scraps of the same recording are one more voice in the dark. It never says ten, as he skipped it. Scenery: nothing rides on it. The clock block's model is a placeholder.

nodes.title: The famous wreck's phonograph
nodes.summary: In the bay of the Old Workings' famous wreck, the one with a lamp still lit, a cabin phonograph sings an old French song, crackling, when you come close. A right click switches it off, and it sings again for the next visitor. It cannot be broken or carried off.

nodes.title: The song in the dark
nodes.summary: Far from any radio, the song you learnt in the wreck comes faint out of the dark when a Retained is near and out of sight. Rare, and only ever for a real one. A margin note in the handbook says what to do.

nodes.title: Hard landings
nodes.summary: The hull takes damage from the sink speed at landing, with a crash and a line naming it; a pilot who taps the rotor lands unhurt from any height.

nodes.title: Brake with the rotor
nodes.summary: Holding the sink speed under 14 blocks a second costs fuel and saves the hull.

nodes.title: The void below
nodes.summary: Before the drill breaks into open space, it sounds hollow for the last two rows, and the crust warning adds what a free fall into the drop under the crust would cost. Brake with the rotor, or pay.

nodes.title: Cavity sensing
nodes.summary: The scanner shows open space under the pod and its depth, and the HUD says when the drop would land hard.

nodes.title: Breakout arrest
nodes.summary: A brace tier that patches for the drop too, or a part that fires the rotor after the last crust row, so a cave landing no longer needs the pilot.

nodes.title: The breach crust
nodes.summary: Three rows of hard rock at each layer floor: 8 hull a row, 24 in all, and heat.

nodes.title: Crust warning
nodes.summary: An amber line within 16 slabs of the crust says how much hull you have and what it will take, with the landing of a drop into open space under it.

nodes.title: Breach brace
nodes.summary: At rest above the crust the brace burns the cheapest ore to patch hull. Crafted as a brace unit and fitted by use, never sold. Fits every chassis.

nodes.title: Cave-ins and quakes
nodes.summary: A blast near a person on foot shakes the roof over them: it creaks for three seconds, then the rock falls and blocks the tunnel, and roof bolts hold what they reach. Quakes will start them too, but nothing does yet; it never deletes built blocks.

nodes.title: Clearing a blockage
nodes.summary: Explosives on foot, a pod charge launcher, crewmates from above, or an emergency teleport.

nodes.title: The regolith slumps
nodes.summary: The loose regolith on top falls like sand when a cut leaves it with nothing under it, so a shallow bore under the skin brings it down into the tunnel. Packed regolith and rock hold, so a deep shaft and the colony pad stand. Slumped regolith never buries the pod: it spills as loose regolith.

nodes.title: The grained crust
nodes.summary: A crust with a vertical grain that flexes on a slow pulse. A drill pushed across it skates, a block placed against it crumbles, a fluid is absorbed, and anything that stops in it is squeezed. It sits at seams and at seed-chosen decoys among the other crusts; for now it is a block placed by hand. Names are placeholders until the lore session.

nodes.title: Dig down along the grain
nodes.summary: The drill skates across the grain but bores straight down along it, as in any rock.

nodes.title: Keep moving
nodes.summary: A pod that is moving or drilling takes no squeeze, so the crust is crossed and never parked on.

nodes.title: Decoy grained crusts
nodes.summary: Some crusts that are not seams are grained too, chosen from the world seed, so a grained crust never tells you where a seam is. The first breach stays plain crust, which the handbook teaches. Nothing in the live game is a decoy until layer 3 gives the world a second boundary.

nodes.title: Heat, pressure and flooding
nodes.summary: Later layers add heat (the Magma Belt), pressure and flooding (the Drowned Deep) that the hull and radiator must answer.

nodes.title: Stranded
nodes.summary: Out of fuel, the pod is powered off and dark until rescue or a reserve tank.

nodes.title: Refuel by hand
nodes.summary: Right-click the pod with coal (2 litres), charcoal (1) or biofuel (3). Solid fuel is for the field, with no pump: stacks of 16, heavy, and sooty. Biofuel is fermented from stalk mash.

nodes.title: Engine soot
nodes.summary: Solid fuel soots the engine. Past a few litres it loses speed and burns more, and at the limit it limps (30% of the speed, twice the burn) but never stops. Once the repair station works, a limp pod will not launch from the colony until serviced.

nodes.title: Service the engine
nodes.summary: The repair station clears the soot for $10 a litre, which lets a limp pod launch again. An account short of the bill buys the whole litres it pays for.

nodes.title: Scrape the flue
nodes.summary: A limp pod at the colony with no money for a service: wait a minute at the repair station and the scrape, free, leaves it just under the limit, able to launch and still slow.

nodes.title: Reserve tank
nodes.summary: A tank crafted from iron and a bucket that restarts a stranded pod.

nodes.title: Company recovery
nodes.summary: A pilot stranded with no fuel item, no reserve and no money is not stuck: after a minute in the dark the Company winch crew hauls pod and pilot home for a fee of $30 a layer deep, taken from the account up to what it holds, then from the hull. The ore in the bay stays behind. The HUD counts the minute down.

nodes.title: The tow line
nodes.summary: Hold a tow cable and right-click another pod; the towed pod hangs below and behind on a 5 block line, across breaches.

nodes.title: Wrecks
nodes.summary: A pod with no hull goes dark where it fell, with its cargo, and its owners are told.

nodes.title: Continuity Event
nodes.summary: Dying cuts to black and silence; your last sound skips like a record, a skull of the Company's own words laughs at you, then RETURN TO WORK. Chat files it with your event number, the cause and the depth; your crew hear your lamp click out and see your body go up in ash and smoke as it stands still and fades. What drops and where you wake are unchanged.

nodes.title: A chain, not smoke
nodes.summary: The tow line is a real chain of links on a sagging curve: it hangs when slack, goes straight when pulled, and shows in the dark of a layer.

nodes.title: Wrecked prefabs that drop salvage
nodes.summary: Ruined buildings and vehicles in the world that give scrap when broken.

nodes.title: Outposts at depth
nodes.summary: A charter crafts an outpost kit and unfolds a lit steel hall at the layer 1 floor, over the breach, with a fuel pump and a sell terminal; every layer 2 run starts there with a full tank. Beds and storage come later.

nodes.title: Environment ratings
nodes.summary: Each depth rates heat, pressure, flooding and quakes, and every block states what it holds. Layers 1 and 2 ask nothing; ratings bite from layer 3, where the block in your hand reads HOLDS HERE or WILL NOT HOLD UNATTENDED for the spot you aim at.

nodes.title: The suit timer
nodes.summary: On foot where the depth asks something, your suit runs on a 3 minute reserve that drains faster with heat, pressure and water. A powered pod seat or a sound outpost hall refills it. At zero the suit breaches and hurts, after an amber and a red warning. Layers 1 and 2 ask nothing.

nodes.title: The outpost that leaks
nodes.summary: An outpost whose shell has a block below its depth's heat, pressure or flooding rating is never destroyed, but heat and water leak in: the suit timer keeps running inside, at half the outside rate, and drips show it.

nodes.title: The risk line
nodes.summary: One line under the header of an outpost's fuel pump and sell terminal says whether the shell holds, or what leaks and how many blocks; it is hidden where the depth asks nothing.

nodes.title: Suit tracks
nodes.summary: Buy your suit heat, pressure and air tiers at the repair station: they raise what it holds against heat, pressure and flooding and how long its reserve lasts, from layer 3 down.

nodes.title: Air canister
nodes.summary: Adds a minute of reserve to your suit, anywhere; never past full.

nodes.title: Teleport pads
nodes.summary: Paired pads a charter builds, at a power cost that grows with depth and mass; nothing mined teleports.

nodes.title: Anchor mode
nodes.summary: A parked Behemoth unfolds into a walkable temporary outpost.

nodes.title: Dynamite
nodes.summary: A 3 by 3 by 3 blast round the pod's feet, one slab deep, for a blocked shaft or a known gas pocket. $100.

nodes.title: Reserve fuel tank
nodes.summary: A bought reserve tank that restarts a stranded pod. $100.

nodes.title: Hull repair nanobots
nodes.summary: Patches the hull. $345.

nodes.title: Plastic explosives
nodes.summary: A 5 by 5 by 5 blast round the pod's feet, two slabs deep. $300.

nodes.title: Quantum teleporter
nodes.summary: Sends you to the nearest pad or the surface; you drop your cargo. $690.

nodes.title: Matter transmitter
nodes.summary: A dearer way home, with the same drop. $1,390.

nodes.title: Pilot
nodes.summary: The legs: movement, flight, fuel.

nodes.title: Passengers
nodes.summary: A seat with no job is allowed: the Prospector's second seat now doubles as the navigator's seat.

nodes.title: Navigator
nodes.summary: The eyes: the second seat pings active sonar, which costs power and is loud; the echoes are ambiguous (ore, gas, empty cave, something that moved) and the navigator marks targets on the pilot's HUD.

nodes.title: Operator
nodes.summary: The hands: a manipulator arm and a charge launcher; a turret later.

nodes.title: Robots fill empty seats
nodes.summary: A component that fills the navigator or operator seat with less skill.

nodes.title: Tender runs and spotting
nodes.summary: One pod brings fuel and empty bays to a pod that keeps drilling; a second pod scans ahead.

nodes.title: Crew beacon
nodes.summary: A pod or suit upgrade that shows where your crewmates are by bearing, so a crew that split up can find each other again. It brings back what vanilla's locator bar did, in the Company's voice.

nodes.title: Altimeter
nodes.summary: Depth in feet, computed from the layer offset plus local height; each layer has its own trick.

nodes.title: Pod status readout
nodes.summary: Hull, fuel and cargo in the corner, with warning lines (HULL BURNING, SEEPAGE, CRUST).

nodes.title: Account readout
nodes.summary: The charter's money, shown on the HUD.

nodes.title: Block readout
nodes.summary: A small line just above the hotbar, clear of the held item name, names the block you look at, with a hint for the ones that need a method: pod drill only, right-click to use, to read, for a ration, to search. It never names what the block hides.

nodes.title: Scanner map
nodes.summary: A side-view slice with ore, lava and gas in their own colours.

nodes.title: Breach fade
nodes.summary: The screen fades as the pod crosses a breach.

nodes.title: Transmission overlay
nodes.summary: Employer messages on a green CRT screen that types out its text.

nodes.title: Green-screen terminal panels
nodes.summary: Every terminal is two blocks high and stands on the ground: a Company cabinet under a big mid-century CRT monitor with bulged glass, brass knobs and a vented casing, its green screen in a riveted bezel with a status strip.

nodes.title: Skins
nodes.summary: Colours, sizes and timings are theme data; a resource pack restyles them with F3+T.

nodes.title: Load gauge and OVERLOADED lamp
nodes.summary: The cockpit's LOAD bar shows the pod's weight against the most it can climb with, the limit marked in red; at the mark the bar turns red, a lamp lights and the plate says OVERLOADED.

nodes.title: The Ribbon cockpit HUD
nodes.summary: While seated, a slim ribbon of gauges and warning lamps along the screen edge replaces the vanilla hotbar and shows the pod's readout lines, warnings included.

nodes.title: Front camera
nodes.summary: A part that turns the cab window into a video feed, clear to the edges, that lava can cook and static can cut.

nodes.title: A dusk sky that never reaches day
nodes.summary: A visual timeline sky swinging between dusk and deep night.

nodes.title: Textures from recipes
nodes.summary: Every 16 pixel texture is generated from data by tools/textures; no hand-painted files to drift.

nodes.title: Placeholder sound
nodes.summary: The drones, the hymn, the pod engines, the drill, the terminals and the UI chirps are ours, built from recipes; the rest are vanilla stand-ins, and a private audio pack carries the original sounds for friends.

nodes.title: Lighting art
nodes.summary: Glow accents and beams; see Darkness and sight.

nodes.title: Salvage looks
nodes.summary: The salvage crate is the freight crate, with the low sled crate as an alternative resource pack; the fungal stalk is the shelf fungus. The other looks are gone.

nodes.title: A public release
nodes.summary: A name, a licence and a soundtrack the project may publish; Modrinth, with its AI-content disclosure.
